page: Microsoft Azure NG8ads_V620_v1 is a GPU-accelerated virtual machine based on an AMD x86_64 architecture operating under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance provides 8 dedicated vCPUs alongside 16.0 GB of system memory, establishing a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per core. Acceleration is handled by a fractional AMD Radeon PRO V620 GPU, assigning a 0.25 partition of the physical graphics processor and 8 GB of dedicated video memory to the host.

Data-intensive local caching and scratch tasks are supported by 1235 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage, and the instance is capable of attaching Premium Storage volumes. Network configurations do not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses, necessitating virtual networks or secondary IP allocation for inbound external connectivity. The CPU environment delivers dedicated cores without virtualized hardware extensions such as AVX-512 or AMX.

Partitioning the AMD V620 GPU provides cost efficiency by eliminating the expense of a full discrete GPU for moderate visual workloads. While the 16.0 GB system memory and 8 GB VRAM boundary limit the instance from handling heavy large-language model training, the balance of NVMe storage and fractional graphics acceleration fits virtual desktop infrastructure (VDI), cloud workstation rendering, video encoding pipelines, and lightweight machine learning inference.
description: Microsoft Azure NG8ads_V620_v1 is a GPU-accelerated virtual machine designed for visual computing and entry-level graphics workloads. Running on an x86_64 AMD processor under Microsoft Hyper-V, the instance is configured with 8 dedicated vCPUs and 16.0 GB of system memory, providing a 2.0 GB per core allocation. Hardware acceleration is provided by a 0.25 fractional AMD Radeon PRO V620 GPU equipped with 8 GB of VRAM. For fast local storage, the instance includes a bundled 1235 GB NVMe SSD that delivers low-latency scratch disk capabilities. Fractional GPU allocation allows users to obtain dedicated graphics acceleration at lower operational cost than full-die alternatives, avoiding idle capacity on modest tasks. This hardware profile is structured for cloud gaming sessions, virtual desktop infrastructure (VDI), interactive 3D rendering, video encoding, and lightweight machine learning inference pipelines that fit within an 8 GB video memory footprint.
